entries.title: Psalms 4:1
segments: This psalm was probably written on the same occasion as

. 
 
The gracious answers which God in times past has granted to the prayers of his people, encourage them to continue to call upon him, especially in distress, expecting that he will hear and relieve them.

entries.title: Psalms 4:2
segments:
My glory; my kingly dignity conferred upon me by God. 
 
  Leasing; lies.

entries.title: Psalms 4:3
segments: Set apart him that is godly; David doubtless refers immediately to himself, as the anointed king of Israel; but the language applies to all who are doing their duty in the sphere to which God has called them.

entries.title: Psalms 4:4
segments:
In awe; of God. 
 
  Be still; cease from your attacks upon me, and quietly submit yourselves to God, who has appointed me to be your king. 
 
Acquaintance with one's own heart is essential to a right understanding of our wants as sinners, and of the way of life by faith in Jesus Christ.

entries.title: Psalms 4:6
segments:
Any good; real, substantial happiness. 
 
Satisfying enjoyment can be found only in doing the will of God, and in his love.

entries.title: Psalms 4:7
segments: Put gladness in my heart; through loving, trusting in, obeying thee, while thou liftest upon me the light of thy countenance.
